stem: Batteries of type $A$ are known to have a mean life of 150 hours. It is required to test whether a new type of battery, type $B$, has a shorter mean life than type $A$ batteries.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Give a reason for using a sample rather than the whole population in carrying out this test.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: A random sample of 120 type $B$ batteries are tested and it is found that their mean life is 147 hours, and an unbiased estimate of the population variance is 225 hours$^2$.
parts.text: Test, at the 2% significance level, whether type $B$ batteries have a shorter mean life than type $A$ batteries.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Calculate a 94% confidence interval for the population mean life of type $B$ batteries.
